newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-STRANSKY SAYS SPRINGBOKS WILL OUTPACE LIONS.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-STRANSKY SAYS SPRINGBOKS WILL OUTPACE LIONS.

text.p: Former Springbok fly-half Joel Stransky believes the British Lions will struggle in both the provincial games and the tests when they embark on their first tour of South Africa for 17 years.

"I would say that what is going to catch the Lions, especially in the first test and in a lot of the provincial games, is the speed of the game," said Stransky, who has had recent first-hand experience of English club rugby at Leicester.
"The South African players will be peaking, they'll be rip-roaring and ready for the challenge. I think it will be very, very tough to beat the Springboks.
"I actually think the Lions might do better in the tests than they do in the provincial games. By the time the tests come they'll have had a few matches together, they'll be gelling."

Stransky, who kicked the winning points for South Africa in the 1995 World Cup final, remains convinced there is a significant gap between southern and northern hemisphere rugby, enhanced by the intense competition of the Super 12 provincial competition.
But while he rates the Lions' chances of a series victory as slim, he suggested the Springboks should beware the Lions' midfield and their captain Martin Johnson.
"I think one of the Lions' great strengths is the centres and I think that is where they might look to play a lot of the game. Any team, if you are really clever, can be broken down."
As for his Leicester team mate Johnson, Stransky commented: "I think the bigger, the harder the game, the more Johnno enjoys it. He will stamp his ability on the southern hemisphere as well."
The Lions fly out on Saturday and play their first match against an Eastern Province invitation XV on May 24.
